%(insertion_open)sThousands of years later, the blueprints of this vehicle somehow ended up in the hands of the Tech-priests.%(insertion_close)s

They finished the design and built new vehicles that satisfied the requirements of the soldiers of the Mordian Iron Guard. The vehicles of the 12th Mordian Armored Regiment proved themselves in battles (however, according to the documents, this regiment consisted of only the Leman Russ tanks).

Björn. Yes, I think that was my name before. I lived in a small village in the North. Father would take me hunting with him all the time. He knew how much I hated it, of course: the tracking, the shooting, the killing. Every day, my heart grew darker and filled with unexplainable anger. Eventually, the thing that was meant to happen happened. It was as though I had wanted to get lost in this dark forest myself. My last memory of my human life is of a shaman who appeared as if out of thin air. Oh yes, I'll never forget that curse. No living soul dares go here because of it, and for good reason. Now, there is only one hunter in this forest. No human or beast is welcome here. This is my home, and my fangs and claws will welcome anyone who dares cross its threshold. I know what, or rather who, they're looking for here. But little Björn is long gone, and they definitely won't like what he's become.
An all-season style dedicated to the elemental power of wind.

"Know, friend, that though I am invisible, I am everywhere. The ancients worshiped me through their spirits and deities, for their journeys, their harvests, their seasons—all depended on my benevolence. I am the breath that gives this Earth life. The elemental force that shapes our very existence. I am action, I am change, bringing motion and purpose to our world: the spirit that stirs the leaves in the ancient forests, that raises the seas, that sculpts cliffs and carves canyons. I cascade through mountains and sweep across great oceans, cross arid deserts and dance over barren steppes. I am the dizzying tempest, the towering cyclone, the whisper that births storms."
Hot dam! Celebrate the heroes of the wetlands with this earthy all-season style.

The maps of World of Tanks are home to some stunning scenery: lush forests, rolling hills, winding rivers. But when the shells stop flying and the smoke of battle clears, a different kind of operation starts to unfold. From the remote corners where tankers seldom tread emerges an army of buck-toothed warriors. Industrious and resourceful, these crafty critters move unseen, building dams and trimming trees to preserve the pristine vistas with the kind of teamwork that would put the most seasoned Platoons to shame. It's not for nothing beavers are known as "nature's engineers."

The great northern forest extends as far as the eye can see, and then a little further. In the shadow of towering pine trees sits a solitary tent: the warm glow of a nearby fire illuminates the clearing, its wisps of smoke billowing over the forest canopy into the falling night. As the flames crackle and pop, the wanderer seated beside it gazes warily into the darkness beyond. In the vast wilderness, where human feet have had no cause to tread, roam the beasts who have guarded this land for as long as the trees have been standing, tall and proud. This is bear country.
Deck out your vehicle like a race car with this all-season style.

On your marks, get set... roll out! Sure, your vehicle was made for the battlefield, but what if it dreams of the glamor and prestige of the world of motorsports? Think about it: when you're fighting for your life, it's fun to imagine the roar of artillery fire is actually from a cheering crowd. And what if, just once, yet another round of grueling emergency field repairs could be swapped for a luxurious pit-stop pampering? Yeah... Not likely. Well, at least you can surprise your trusty tank with a fresh coat of paint inspired by stylish race cars.
Wrap your vehicle in an all-season style that was millennia in the making.

Timeless and radiant, copper is deeply intertwined with the rise of human civilization. From primitive tools to sacred art, its warm glow and versatility influenced mythology and trade, marking the dawn of metallurgy and shaping the material world for our ancestors. Revered by ancient cultures and still essential today, it was only a matter of time before this immortal vein flowed into your armor. The metal of gods and empires endures—reforged for the modern warrior.

Following successful trials for the Black Prince tank, the decision was made to continue the trials on the front. Several tanks were sent to the 79th Armored Division, which had vast experience in using experimental and unusual vehicles, generally called Hobart's Funnies. During their operation, the vehicles became quite shabby and were equipped with body kits.
An all-season style for those who are used to standing in lines during annual Black Friday sales.

You can't see me! Oh, wait, you can? Huh. Must not have changed color yet. How do I do it? Oh, I get asked that all the time. Honestly, I don't even know. It's something to do with my pigment, or something. And you're telling me you have to specifically conceal your tank so people don't see you? Like, using special equipment and camouflages and stuff? Wow. That's crazy...anyway, I'd best get going. I've got people to meet and flies to catch. Now you see me, now you don't!

"King of the festival? Oh, you flatter me! I'm literally just a TD. Let me tell you, though, this festival is something special. It's about community, one united by a common interest and a shared passion. If you're a tank enthusiast, you're welcome here—that's something worth celebrating. And look, since you've so kindly named me king of the festival, then here's a little something for you to remember the occasion by. Put it on whatever vehicle you want—trust me, even the rustiest old hunk of junk will get a new shine in this bad boy. Once again, thank you for joining this year's festivities. Now let the celebrations begin!"
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass: Season 4.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass: Season 4.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass: Season 4.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season V.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season V.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season VI.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season V.
An all-season style awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season VII.

An all-season style dedicated to the secret bunker expedition. Kittel, Mancini, and Holmberg found numerous parts for battle vehicles and thousands of large-caliber machine gun rounds. They believed this scrap was an echo of war—but only before they discovered the objective of their mission.

An all-season style reminding us of how dangerous and violent the desert can be. Infernal heat, parasites, wild animals, and venomous insects will stick for a long time with Rebecca Holmberg, who believed it could not get any worse. As it turned out, it always could.

An all-season style depicting an oasis found by Kittel after a four-day march across sand waves. The long-awaited rest was interrupted by a ferocious lion's roar, who was ready to attack but suddenly stopped before the translator and looked at him as though he had met an old friend. Emil understood: The local fauna will not bother them anymore.

An all-season style depicting three domesticated camels brought by Sandro Mancini after he went looking for water. Rebecca and Emil never learned how exactly this adventure seeker managed to get his hands on the animals, but those ships of the desert saved their lives when the group's vehicles got buried in the sands forever.
An all-season style to help remain hidden in lush jungle environments.

The jungle, as it turned out, was full of surprises for wildlife enthusiast Tomasz, whose animated reactions to creatures he had never seen in the flesh before greatly amused his crewmates. One morning, as he clambered absent-mindedly onto his tank's commander's hatch, he let out a startled shout at the sight of an unusually large lizard sunning itself on the roof. The lizard quickly scrambled away, but Tomasz's cry of "Jaszczurka! Jakie bydlę!" remained a favorite in-joke of his crew for months thereafter.
An all-season style designed to blend with the rich green hues of the tropical rainforest.

An avid reader from a literary family, Konrad had only experienced jungles through the pages of classic novels, where they were often portrayed as dark and foreboding—an image that was shattered the moment he first rolled through their rich canopy of colors. He still dreams of writing a great work about the vast mountain forests of his home, but his second book, he insists, will honor the bright, primordial beauty of the jungle.
An all-season style for camouflage among the dense thickets of the jungle.

There was little Wataru enjoyed more than keeping his teammates on their toes through practical jokes. During one expedition far from base, an unusually panicked-sounding Wataru radioed in a warning: an enraged elephant, he said, was charging in his teammates' direction. As they anxiously scanned the trees, bracing to face the rampaging beast, they were bombarded with a rain of bananas hurled from the underbrush—where Wataru was in fits of laughter at the crew who had fallen for his false alarm.
An all-season style that pays tribute to the extreme testing conditions of the jungle.

A seasoned communications expert and skilled negotiator, Angélique had faced intense missions before—but the jungle presented an entirely new challenge. The trials had been framed as a competition for the best international tankers, but she knew the real stakes—and that, in the sweltering heat and oppressive humidity, tensions could boil over at any moment. All it would take was one spark to ignite chaos—and she had to draw on all her expertise to make sure that didn't happen.
An all-season style dedicated to the unstoppable Duke Nukem.

Arrogant? Damn right he is, and what of it? You'd be arrogant too if you were Duke. It's not his fault he was blessed with such dashing good looks—or such big guns. Many have tried to challenge him, and they've all been blasted into oblivion. He's an equal opportunity ass kicker who doesn't discriminate—and if you mess with the best, you'll die like the rest. So what do you say? Gonna come get some? Because Duke came to kick ass and chew bubble gum. And he's all outta gum.
An all-season style dedicated to the most iconic enemies in the Duke Nukem universe.

Duke's seen it all. Over countless missions, he's fought just about every menace imaginable—aliens, Octabrains, sentries, sharks, and reptilian foot soldiers of all shapes and sizes. There’s no enemy too dangerous for Duke, but if there’s one thing he hates, it’s pigs: big, dumb, and ugly as hell, they just keep coming. Fortunately for Duke, they make perfect cannon fodder—just the way he likes it. When it's time for a hog hunt, you can bet your ass Duke's gonna be making' bacon.

An all-season style dedicated to the movie Rambo: First Blood.

Haunted by memories of serving in Vietnam, former Green Beret John Rambo roams the country in search of peace and purpose. But when a run-in with a small-town sheriff leads to his imprisonment, Rambo is left with much more than he bargained for. The unexpected target of a huge manhunt, he must draw on all his combat expertise and survival instincts as he fights his pursuers—and his own demons.

An all-season style dedicated to the movie Rambo: First Blood Part II.
RAMBO: FIRST BLOOD PART II ™ & © 1985 STUDIOCANAL S.A.S. All Rights Reserved. © 2025 STUDIOCANAL S.A.S. (R) All Rights Reserved.

Languishing in jail years after his one-man war against the law in Hope, Rambo is offered a shot at release and redemption. The condition? Carry out a top-secret solo mission in the one place he vowed never to return—Vietnam. Deep behind enemy lines, in thick jungles where danger lurks in every shadow, Rambo is again forced to confront his past and use every ounce of his combat skills to survive.

An all-season style dedicated to the movie Rambo III.
RAMBO III ™ & © 1988 STUDIOCANAL S.A.S. All Rights Reserved. © 2025 STUDIOCANAL S.A.S. (R) All Rights Reserved.

After years of brutal combat and inner turmoil, Rambo seems to be on the path to a more peaceful life. That is, until his former commanding officer Colonel Trautman is captured—and Rambo has no option but to act. Determined to save his friend and mentor, he embarks on a one-man mission through war-torn Afghanistan, forging unlikely alliances as he battles overwhelming odds and formidable foes.
Honor Detroit's finest with this explosive all-season style.

"It's a free society—except there ain't nothin' free, because there's no guarantees, y'know? You're on your own. It's the law of the jungle."

There's no denying it: the city has seen better days. Crime is at a record high, and being a cop is more dangerous than ever... but that won't stop these intrepid officers. When every shift could be your last, there's no room for mistakes. No matter how bleak things look out there, they keep pushing back against the cutthroat gangs of Old Detroit. Because if they don't... there will be trouble.
Somewhere there is a crime happening. Lay down the law in this cybernetically enhanced all-season style.

"Serve the public trust. Protect the innocent. Uphold the law."

These are the prime directives hardcoded in the mind of Alex Murphy, a police officer resurrected and reborn as RoboCop, the ultimate law enforcement unit. Encased in titanium and Kevlar, there's little left of the man Murphy once was—at least on the surface. But his drive to bring criminals to justice survived the transformation from man to machine, and breaking the law just got a whole lot more dangerous. You'd better stay out of trouble if you value your freedom... or your life.
An all-season style brought to you by Omni Consumer Products.

"Old Detroit has a cancer. The cancer is crime, and it must be cut out before we employ the two million workers that will breathe life into this city again."

The CEO of Omni Consumer Products dreamed of transforming Old Detroit into Delta City: a gleaming utopia meant to replace the grime and lawlessness of the urban hellscape his city had become. It might sound like a noble idea, but cleaning up a mess like that costs more than just truckloads of cash—it means turning a blind eye to corruption and privatizing justice.
An all-season style dedicated to Lara Croft's adventurous spirit.

"Adventure is all around us, wherever we look. Sometimes we seek it out—and sometimes it finds us. You might think you're not ready for it, but trust me—you are. The world is full of unanswered questions, unexplained mysteries, and forgotten stories. What could be more human than the drive to seek answers? That thirst for knowledge, that lust for discovery—it lives in all of us, even if we don't know it, so embrace the journey. Adventure awaits."
An all-season style dedicated to the mysteries of distant lands.

"Even tattered fragments like this hold stories waiting to be uncovered. The contours of a far-off land: rugged, mountainous—perhaps dangerous. Ancient, cryptic runes, hinting at a forgotten civilization. A people with customs, beliefs, and a way of life all their own. Once rich, proud, thriving—now long since lost to the ravages of time. People forget, but maps remember. Even in ruin, they offer glimpses of what once was—and what may still be found."
An all-season style with a muted green and gray camouflage design.

Exuberant and boisterous off the battlefield, something would change in Matthew the moment he climbed into the commander's hatch. The descendant of immigrants who'd grafted hard to carve out their place in America, he'd been raised with the firm belief that there was a time for laughter and a time for honest work; as his grandda used to tell him, "You'll never plow a field by turning it over in your mind." Whenever uncertainty crept in, Matthew remembered those words, and reminded himself that the best way to solve any problem was to act—quickly, decisively, and without a moment's hesitation.
An all-season style with earthy green and brown tones for camouflage in natural environments.

For Angus, shooting is meditative—be it through the sights of a rifle or the twin barrels of a heavy tank. As soon as that first shot lands—and, with Angus, it always does—there's no distracting him. It's as though he's back hunting on the windswept moors of the Highlands, unperturbed by wild rains, howling winds, or bloodthirsty midges. He liked his nickname, Cannon, but couldn't help but feel it did him a disservice. Cannons are loud and unpredictable. He's far more precise than that.
An all-season style that resembles a birds-eye view of meandering rivers.

All the tankers selected for the trials were serious—the very best of their nations' respective tanking schools, with years of experience under their belts. But none had encountered anyone quite like Wei Jian. By day, he would carry a notepad in hand, meticulously checking every adjustment to his gear, every shift in the wind. By night, long after the barracks fell silent, he would sit hunched over his notes under the dim light of a flashlight until the early hours of the morning. They say the devil is in the details. But for Wei Jian, everything was in the details.
An abstract all-season style with a striking high-contrast color scheme.

Alessia's serene, almost ethereal presence caught many of her competitors off guard. During downtime, they would find her meditating in the forest behind the barracks, listening to the birdsong—even when the rain soaked her to the skin. They didn't know what to think, but they knew that someone so calm and detached would be eaten alive on the battlefield. Or so they thought—until they saw her in action. Conditions worsened and tensions frayed, but Alessia's focus never wavered. Whatever she'd been contemplating in the forest, it was damn well working.
An all-season style for what comes after the dead start walking.

"I used to beg for quiet. Couldn't stand all that city racket—folks running their mouths like they had something worth saying, music blasting, engines screaming down the street... It's quiet now. All you hear are the cicadas and the crows. That is, if you're lucky, anyway. Otherwise, you hear the walkers—their hungry growls. Yeah... I used to hate all that noise. Now I miss it."
Face a grisly new reality in this all-season style.

"Thought you were gonna have it easy, huh? Good job, nice house, fancy neighborhood. That's all gone now. The dead make every day a struggle, and the living are the ones you really gotta be afraid of. Every day's a test, and most folks won’t make it. Welcome to the new world."
An ominous all-season style. Don't get too close to this one...

"Feels like a lifetime ago, waking up in that hospital bed. No doctors, no nurses, just a whole lot of blood and smashed up gear, lights flickering. The place stank of rot. I came across a pair of chained-up doors: DON'T OPEN DEAD INSIDE was painted across 'em. Wasn't ‘til later I truly understood what that meant. Whoever was in that room... they'd already died once. That should've been enough."
An all-season style suited to the toughest of boreal expeditions.

"I was assigned to investigate concerning radio signals from an unregistered, highly remote transmission station. I have no doubt that we will decipher the message and locate its precise origin soon enough, but I can't shake the feeling that what we find won't be cause for celebration. Whoever and whatever may be waiting for us, we must proceed carefully. As we like to say in my line of work, dead air is better than a dead operator."
The ideal all-season style for an intrepid investigator.

"When they said there was a signal no one could account for, I packed my equipment and headed north as soon as I could. I'll admit it, crossing the tundra in a tank wasn't exactly how I pictured my next assignment. I'm more at home behind my bench than a periscope, but this is certainly one way of seeing the world—and it's hard not to be curious about what we'll find. Maybe it's nothing. Maybe not. Either way, I'll be among the very first to know."
Channel an erudite engineer in this all-season style.

"To me, this mission is an exercise in skill. Whatever these signals represent, they can be understood—and that is what matters. I find comfort in the order of it all, in the mathematics that underpin the mystery. For now, I am utterly focused on the intellectual challenge at hand, and I am relishing every second. Perhaps it seems that I am a simple man, but I simply love my craft. The world only makes sense when my dials align."
An all-season style befitting a stoic scout.

"I've got no idea what we might find up here, but I've got all the intel I need: there's a signal, and we're out here to track it. The equipment's solid, the terrain's less so, and the weather's doing its best to bury both. But that's all part of the job. I've worked in worse, and I trust my team with my life... but let's hope it doesn't come to that. In any case, whoever's out there, they're talking to someone—and we can't go home until we find out who."
A sandy all-season style for blending into a sea of dunes.

Soft citadels of rising gold,

By unseen architects of old.

Golden ramparts greet the sun,

By evening, none remain undone.

They shift, they drift, they softly sweep,

An amber tide in restless sleep.
Brace against the desert wind in this tactical all-season style.

A ripple threads the heated air,

Then it strips the desert bare.

The daylight dims to copper haze,

The world ablur amid the blaze.

It howls, it blinds, it scours the sands,

Leaving windswept, altered lands.
An all-season style based on the vast North African expanse.

A white sun crowns the barren land,

Its scepter forged of rock and sand.

No border breaks the endless plain,

No respite found in shade or rain.

And when the daylight yields its throne,

The night ascends to rule alone.
Chart the rocky desert plateaus with this geological all-season style.

Bare stone beneath a burning sky,

Where ancient seas have long run dry.

The gods have carved with patient hand

A fortress from the stubborn land.

Each fractured ridge, each splintered seam,

Is part of a far greater scheme.
Add some island flair to the battlefield with this tropical all-season style.

Working freelance boat charters out in Micronesia is a pretty sweet life. Beats the hell out of my stint in Special Forces, that's for sure—now I'm just ferrying reporters between little-known islands, wind in my hair and a handgun riding easy in my pocket. Yeah... it's a pretty chill gig. Huh, why the handgun? Well, I guess some old habits die hard. Besides, you never know what might be waiting for you out here. Let's just say I've seen what can happen when a job goes sideways, and I don't plan on being caught off guard again.
Go native in this primal all-season style.

"The jungle speaks through the warrior. The Path leads to the heart of the jungle. Follow the Path and you will find the answer."

The jungle creeps under your skin, whispering through your senses. And as your memory of civilization fades, you realize that the world is governed by older laws. Survival gnaws at the edges of your reason until raw instinct claws its way to the surface—and you'd better hope it doesn't fail you. But be warned: the longer you follow the Path, the less of the man you once were remains.
Walk the path of the warrior with this tribal all-season style.

"As you become stronger, with each new skill you learn, the tatau will grow.

That's what I was told when I woke up and saw the fresh ink burned into my arm. Is it really this tattoo giving me strength I never had? Or was all of this already inside me, just waiting to come out? None of it makes sense. A few days ago, I was just some slacker from California. Now I'm out here surviving, fighting... killing. And I've never felt so alive. Maybe I'm losing my mind. Or maybe this is who I was supposed to be all along. A warrior. A true Rakyat. 'Cause for the first time ever, I feel like I'm home."
Don this all-season style to suit up your vehicle for Salieri's neighborhood.

The streets of Little Italy are narrow, lined with soot-stained brick buildings whose windows are perpetually hazed with smoke. Laundry swings overhead from clotheslines strung between balconies, carrying the faint scent of tomato sauce. Around here, the man you're shooting the breeze with over a Swift Cola one day might be the one shooting you in the back the next. If those walls could talk, they'd have plenty to say—but they would never rat out the hardworking businessmen who make their deals in the shadowed corners.
Harness the raw speed of the Lost Heaven Grand Prix in this high-octane all-season style.

"See the fastest racers on Earth! Feel the rumble as they head up the home straight! Experience speed like never before!"

September 4th, 1932. A beautiful Sunday morning. The skies are clear, the motors are on the grid, and the Lost Heaven Grand Prix is about to begin.

There's just one problem. The Don's driver, Mikey Dunne, has suffered a mysterious last-minute injury. With no time to spare, Tommy Angelo is called to take the wheel—and beat the European hotshot Lichtenberg, backed by Morello. What Tommy doesn't know, though, is that even if he wins the race, the war is just beginning...
Deliver Don Salieri's regards to all who wrong you in this atmospheric all-season style.

"Maybe I should have taken off when I had the chance. But I couldn't go back to being a nobody."

Times are hard in Lost Heaven. The Great Depression has spared no one. Everybody's just trying to get by any way they can, but honest work is hard to come by—while Prohibition has turned the city's criminal underworld into a land of opportunity for those willing to get their hands dirty.

Tommy Angelo never imagined himself living a life like this, but working for Don Salieri pays handsomely and promises a path out of obscurity. The only question is: what will it cost him in the end?
Rip and tear, until it is done. Do it in this all-season, infernal-grade containment suit.

The UAC's most remarkable recent discovery was made on its expedition to Hell's Kadingir Sanctum. The team uncovered a tomb hidden beyond swathes of near-impassable terrain, its entrance and walls inscribed with protective runes and imprisonment incantations. Numerous relics were recovered, among them a suit of unmistakably human proportions. Extracted from the encasing rock and subjected to extensive testing, the artifact proved virtually impervious to damage. Still, a vital component is needed to activate the suit's mystifying power, likely the Doom Slayer himself.
For millennia they have survived. Made others sacrifice in the name of their prosperity. Reclaim their power with this all-season style.

"Earth will be consumed and the energy will continue to flow. It is your people's survival... against mine."

The Maykrs once stood as stewards of a rigid celestial order. But when the wellsprings of their power ran dry, they turned their gaze beyond the veil... and found Hell. In the screaming dark between realms, they forged a pact. Mortal worlds were opened to invasion, countless souls were harvested as energy, and the Maykrs drew upon that power to sustain their fading existence. Thus, an unholy union was born, spreading to consume all things. 

Until the Slayer intervened.
Hurt 'em plenty in this brutal all-season style.

"In the age of fire and ruin, when the legions of Hell first set foot upon Argent D'Nur, another came... an outsider, his path to their world carved in blood, for the demons could not escape his wrath."

The demons swept through mortal realms. Now, another world stood upon the brink of annihilation. The Sentinels fought bravely, yet none could withstand the endless hordes. Except one. They knew neither his name nor his origin. They knew only that he alone possessed the strength to rip and tear their salvation from the maw of damnation. 

And so, when all hope seemed lost, they launched the Slayer.
An improvised all-season style for blending into sandy flatlands.

"For an expedition across miles of nothing but salt flats and wind-blown dunes, our armour sticks out like a sore thumb. More like a brass band in a library, actually. Trouble is, me and the crew haven't exactly got much to work with out here in the "field"—if you can call it that. Still, if there's one thing life as a tanker has taught me, it's to keep calm, carry on, and make do. Well, that's three things, but never mind. Point is, I got hold of some leftover paint and did a halfway decent job, all things considered."
A rugged all-season style for effective cover in barren climes.

"The biting sands stretch endlessly ahead, raw and alien. A world away from the powdery white beaches of my youth in Okinawa. Grains scrape against the hull with every gust, constantly abrading the hastily painted camouflage. Even sealed inside, I can taste the dust. We lurch over another unseen ridge, suspension groaning in protest. I glance at the map again, though it offers little guidance; the horizon remains stubbornly featureless, as if the land itself refuses to acknowledge our presence. Even so, I check the scope again. Empty. Always empty, until it isn't."
An authentic all-season style for mimicking variable battlefield terrain.

"The terrain here still confuses me. It feels strangely empty of water, even with the sea so near. One moment it is dry steppe, the next it breaks into saline flats and crusted ground. It could be quite beautiful under different circumstances, if I were not the one responsible for traversing it...

With little time for thoughts of elegance, I brushed that notion aside and applied camouflage directly onto the starkly exposed hull of my armor: rough, patchy shapes meant to mimic the land's muted palette. It will have to do."
A tactical all-season style, well-suited to exposed plains.

"This land offers little cover. The sand stretches for kilometers, broken only by patches of takir. The ground here cannot be trusted; what appears solid often is not. Our convoy stands out, and camouflage intended for forests and fields has no place here. Without proper supplies, we must use what we have. Applied carefully, a small amount of paint is enough to dull our outline. It is not perfect, but it will be sufficient—it needs only to make us harder to see than those who are looking for us."
An all-season style inspired by the Imperium of Man. Available as part of a special event in collaboration with the Warhammer 40,000 universe.
An all-season style inspired by the Chaos faction. Available as part of a special event in collaboration with the Warhammer 40,000 universe.
An all-season style inspired by the colors of the Order of the Martyred Lady of the Adepta Sororitas faction from the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Available within Battle Pass Season VIII.
An all-season style inspired by the colors of the Death Guard Legion of the Chaos Space Marines faction from the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season VIII.
An all-season style inspired by the colors of the Evil Sunz Clan of the Orks faction from the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season VIII.
An all-season style inspired by the colors of the Ultramarine Chapter of the Adeptus Astartes faction from the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Awarded at a certain Stage of Battle Pass Season VIII.
An all-season style awarded for your achievements during Battle Pass Season IX.

"I know what you're thinking. It's not very sophisticated, I'm well aware. But we don't exactly have a wealth of materials at our disposal. And besides, we've done worse before. Well, we probably have, at least. We know the basic principles, anyway—gather all the conductive material you can find, cobble together something vaguely resembling a Faraday cage, and hope for the best. Will it be enough to protect us? Hard to say. We've done what we can with the materials we had to hand. But, against what we're about to be faced with, would anything be enough to protect us?"

"A Faraday cage, it is called. Or a Faraday shield. Cover an object in conductive material or mesh and, if you have covered it well enough—and your material is conductive enough—any electrical fields it comes into contact with will be channeled and distributed around the outside of it. Meanwhile, whatever is inside will be safe and sound. Make such a cage large enough, and there you can sit—completely protected from the high voltage coursing around the outside, without a care in the world. Is it not a breathtaking thought, that something so remarkable is even possible?"

"Electricity is a beast of dangerous power. It is a force of nature with endless potential and possibilities. And yet, unlike many other forces of nature, it is predictable. It is a tameable beast. It can be subjugated, channeled, or even neutralized through insulation. It is simple science. We may not know all the capabilities of what we are faced with, but we know what precautions we must take, and we take them. We protect ourselves as best we can, according to fundamental scientific principles. And why? Because this is our duty, and there is no other option. If not us, then who?"

"This is what our technology is capable of. This is how far our research can take us. For so long, we have simply used whatever we could find to protect our vehicles against strong electric currents. And by doing so, we have been tempting fate. I have complete faith in our crew and their capabilities, but the more times you take that risk, the higher the chances of disaster become. Now, after all the experiments, prototypes, and makeshift solutions, after all the blood, sweat, and tears, we see the fruits of our labor. Finally, we have created the shield we worked so long to make. Finally, we are prepared."

An all-season style depicting the state of Focht's vehicle that has spent too long in Mirny-13. The town had an effect on the commander, too. Once clear and bright, the scientist's mind started to be filled with visions, voices, and hallucinations. Initially, he tried to note the changes in his journal, but his handwriting got progressively worse, his entries started containing phrases in an unknown language, and his illustrations became increasingly more spine-chilling.

An all-season style depicting the layout of vehicle protection for operations in Mirny-13. Officers insisted that each vehicle in the group be equipped with anti-radiation lining capable of protecting against the worst-case radiation scenario. Their concerns did not play out, but that did not make anyone feel any better.

An all-season style depicting the appearance of the vehicle discovered in Mirny-13 by the second group. The vehicle was standing near one of the Mirium sources, covered in scratches and inscriptions, but with no combat damage and...no crew. Hope spent several nights trying to get at least some information from the soulless metal, but the only result was a surprising sense of calmness and the desire to stay inside the vehicle for as long as possible.

An all-season style created as a reminder of the very first operation in Mirny-13. Back then, nobody knew what the group would encounter in the gloomy, ruined town. That is why, before they headed out, Mariya Lastochkina suggested equipping the vehicles with additional radiation protection. The process was long and monotonous, and the lead negatively affected the crews' health, but receiving a fatal dose of radiation would have been even worse.
An all-season style inspired by the dappled camouflage patterns that adorned British vehicles during the Second World War.

An all-season style inspired by the dappled camouflage patterns that adorned British vehicles during the Second World War. While Arthur was never much of a cartoon person, he did have a soft spot for a certain animated mouse with big ears and a funny voice, whose likeness he and his crewmates eventually started seeing in the spotted patterns of this camouflage.
An all-season style inspired by camouflage patterns used by U.S. forces in northwestern Europe in 1944–45, including on D-Day.

An all-season style inspired by camouflage patterns used by U.S. forces in northwestern Europe in 1944–45, including on D-Day. Jack's extreme confidence ruffled a few feathers when he first arrived in Europe, with his British counterparts perceiving it as arrogance. His outstanding performance in training exercises, however, made them grudgingly admit his confidence may be justified—and, on the beaches of Normandy, he would prove that it was.
An all-season style inspired by camouflage patterns on the vehicles used by the Free French Forces during the Second World War.

An all-season style inspired by camouflage patterns on the vehicles used by the Free French Forces during the Second World War. As a dyed-in-the-wool patriot of France, Louis enjoyed provoking his English-speaking crewmates by telling them the many ways in which he considered his country superior to theirs. But when it came to combat vehicles, even he had to admit that American tanks had a certain je ne sais quoi.
An all-season style that pays tribute to the heroic role played by Allied paratroopers on D-Day.

An all-season style that pays tribute to the heroic role played by Allied paratroopers on D-Day, with thousands of predominantly American, British, and Canadian airborne troops deployed to secure key sites around the beaches below and facilitate the huge amphibious landings that followed.
Brains meet brawn in the scribbled schematics of this all-season style.

Covered in quick sketches and frantic formulas, this style blends math with mayhem. Every chalked line and crude diagram forms a recipe for destruction, showing that true power comes from both mind and muscle. Don this style and turn doodles into domination.
There's no room for error, and no need for luck.

Every number and diagram scrawled on your armor is the result of long hours, trial and error, and a whole lot of coffee. This style is for those who test, tweak, and push their vehicles until they can take whatever the battlefield throws at them. It's not about luck—it's about figuring out exactly what's going to work... and fixing it when it doesn't.
Plans change, but progress marches on.

Out here, blueprints are drawn with broken chalk and desperate hands. Calculations are frantic, armor gets patched up with whatever's around, and every note on the hull keeps the vehicle one step ahead of the scrap heap. Worry about perfection later—this style's about making sure the engine still roars when the dust clears.
Blur the boundaries of what you thought possible.
Born from endless trials and tests, the eye-catching wavy lines of this experimental look represent a whole new wave of destruction.
Feel the ancient might of the Da'at Yichud with this all-season style.

Centuries ago, the secretive Da'at Yichud crafted weapons for a bleak future they prayed would never come—impossible creations, equal parts myth and machine. The enemy discovered a vault where some of these artifacts had been hidden. They twisted what they found, building war machines that brought the world to its knees.

But among the relics left untouched was the Power Suit—impossibly advanced, yet older than any nation still standing. Such technology enhances ordinary armor in ways that defy conventional engineering, giving the Resistance the strength to keep fighting.
An all-season style that champions the pure of heart.

It was a captured enemy vehicle—until Max Hass got creative. A beloved member of the Kreisau Circle and a gentle giant with a heart almost as big as his fists, Max doesn't say much, but he sure knows how to make a statement. Now his messy, childlike scrawl—"HASS 3"—is proudly scribbled across the armor, with bright swirls and butterflies for good measure. Why "3"? Because in Max's eyes, it's a brand new tank. No longer a tool of oppression, it's his buddy now. His steel twin. Max... but on caterpillar tracks. It's cheerful, a little odd, and overflowing with heart. Just like him.
Shatter your opponents' resistance with this sinister all-season style.

"Thus we will see the superiority of the machine over flesh and blood!"

This armor echoes the stark, oppressive aesthetic of a continent-spanning force bent on spreading fear and subjugation. Molded in Deathshead's nightmarish "research facility"—a grim nexus of depravity masquerading as science—each polished surface reflects the austere might of the regime's mechanized legions. Built to crush rebellion and smother hope, behold this dark harbinger of a world where technology blindly serves the will of evil.
An all-season style available during Battle Pass: Judgment Day.
An all-season style, awarded for reaching Rank 15 in Steel Hunter mode.
An all-season style, awarded for reaching Rank 25 in Steel Hunter mode.
An all-season style, developed for the same-name mode.
Perhaps it's best to let some legends remain legends.

"My friend, I must confide in you what has lately disturbed my sleep. Not long ago, our lord had a statue set up in the palace court: a bull of gleaming brass, its belly left hollow. On certain days, when something or, perhaps, someone has greatly vexed the ruler, we servants are instructed to pile wood beneath the beast and kindle a fire. What follows is hidden from our sight, for we are sent away; yet soon the bull fills the palace with dreadful bellowing. The sound is all but human. I cannot help but wonder—does some spirit dwell within the statue, or is it the bull itself that suffers?"
An all-season style developed to commemorate the annual Carnival season.

In many Christian countries, Carnival is held before Lent. The celebration always includes dressing up, taking part in masquerades, and joyful performances. The tradition of parades was born in Europe. On the day of Carnival, folk would hide their faces under masks and go to the city to participate in the massive celebration, singing, dancing, and talking to people from different social groups.
An all-season style dedicated to the biggest country in South America both in terms of territory and population.

Each color of the Brazilian flag has its meaning: green symbolizes the forests, yellow is for natural resources (gold), and the blue circle with constellations represents the sky on the day when Brazil declared itself a republic. The inscription on the white stripe reads "Ordem e Progresso" (Order and Progress), which is used as the name of the style.
An all-season style developed to commemorate the large-scale collaboration of World of Tanks and the band Sabaton in 2021.

Plated armor, introduced in late 14th century, was the pinnacle of blacksmithing in the medieval industry. This protective kit covered almost the entire body of the warrior wearing it—only the plates' joints were relatively vulnerable. Such armor could weigh around 30 kilograms, and its cost could be comparable to that of an entire village. In addition to the obvious protective properties, such armor also had status value. As a rule, plated armor was custom-made, not a mass-produced item.
Embrace the Halloween spirit in this spectral all-season style.

Was that wind in the trees, or the clatter of steel?
Could there be something... else out there?
Each shadow conceals what I hope isn't real,
As I peer through my sights with care.
If a phantom appeared, I admit I'd be scared
As it hovered 'neath the cold moon's light,
But a tank in the dark is a terror compared
To the things that go bump in the night!

An all-season style that remembers all vehicles used by Spain across the 20th century.
Acquired through any WoT Plus tier.

Here's to all vehicles borrowed, recycled, and used by Spain across the 20th century!
In the 1960s and 1970s, regulation camouflage was rare, and tanks were mostly painted in a single color. During military exercises, this improvised camouflage could be applied using mud and then, conveniently, washed off with water.
One of these training sessions in Spain was the inspiration behind Campeador, although this practice existed in various European armies.
Acquired through any WoT Plus tier.

An all-season style inspired by military exercises in the late 20th century, where mud replaced paint as an improvised camouflage.
Acquired through any WoT Plus tier.

In the 1960s and 1970s, regulation camouflage was rare, and tanks were mostly painted in a single color. During military exercises, this improvised camouflage could be applied using mud and then, conveniently, washed off with water.
One of these training sessions was the inspiration behind Campeador, although this practice existed in various armies.
Acquired through any WoT Plus tier.
An all-season style dedicated to the annual celebration of Canada Day.

On July 1, 1867, the colonies of Canada, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick were united into the state of Canada. After a year, governor-general Charles Stanley Monck issued a royal proclamation asking for Canadians to celebrate the anniversary of Confederation and name it Dominion Day in memory of the previous state of the country. Initially, the date was unofficial, but the government started to promote it in the 1980s, when it was renamed Canada Day, became a holiday, and gradually turned into the main national day celebrated throughout the country.
Life is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you're gonna get.

I think back to when I was little. Getting a box of chocolates was what Christmas was all about. I still remember the foil rustling, putting the first chocolate into my mouth, it melting slowly, touching and enveloping my taste buds...a happy child—that's what I was. They're nice memories.

Surf's up! Today, it's just you and the ocean. You gaze out at the vast blue expanse before you, at the waves rising and rolling before crashing onto the soft sands of the shore. One meter. Three meters. Five. Ten...The raw power of nature, surging right before your eyes. You're small against the towering waves, but you're determined and you're focused. Just like you always do, you steady your board, take a deep breath, and paddle out. It's time to catch that wave.
Where there is a box, there is a cat inside it. A common truth.

A box. Another box. More boxes! Am I in heaven? Meow, I'm gonna rustle them all night long! Oh, I see you've pinned your Christmas tree to the floor. Nah, not gonna help. But you still love me, don't you? You DO love me!

"Do you still want multi-turret vehicles? If only you knew how to live with three heads, one of which is always hungry (BONES! MEAT! MORE MEAT!), the other is always sleeping, and I have to move our huge and heavy body and make sure no one escapes from Hades (LIAR! LIAR! DIRTY LIAR! You just watch the gate while I look for our food!).

There she goes again. She always wants to eat. Do you want multi-turret vehicles? Put yourself in my shoes, then we'll talk. (LIAR! Hey, you, wake up, tell her that all three of us have one stomach!)"
A unique all-season style awarded for participating in The Great Race event.
An all-season style based on the colors and emblems of the national flag of the Republic of Chile. The name of the style is taken from the national motto of this country.
An all-season style inspired by the Ancient Roman legionnaire armor.

Triarii were elite warriors in the Ancient Roman army that were usually positioned in the third battle line. They were the most experienced and well-armed soldiers, and were used as a decisive force in battle. Hence, an old Roman saying "it comes down to the triarii" meant carrying on to the bitter end. In battle, they used a phalanx formation that would stop the enemy and allow the first battle lines to regroup. Triarii were armed with spears and large shields. Their equipment also included a gladius, a helmet, metal mail armor and greaves.

To extend the lifespan of the armor, Roman armorers used a process called bluing. When iron was heated, a layer of oxide was created on the surface that would turn it blue, gray, or purple.
An all-season style inspired by the Ancient Roman legionnaire armor.

Hastati were heavy infantry warriors in the Ancient Roman army. Before the battle started, they worked together with velites and threw javelins at the enemy, then proceeded into melee combat. Hastati fought with a short stabbing sword, the gladius. Their armor consisted of a helmet, a square chestplate, greaves and sometimes chainmail. They also used a big oval shield called a scutum.

To extend the lifespan of the armor, Roman armorers used a process called bluing. When iron was heated, a layer of oxide was created on the surface that would turn it blue, gray, or purple.
An all-season style inspired by the Ancient Roman legionnaire armor.

In the Ancient Roman army, velites were light infantry and were considered the most mobile. They were positioned in the first battle line, threw darts at the enemy, and retreated behind the lines. Velites were armed with short swords and used helmets and light round shields for protection.

To extend the lifespan of the armor, Roman armorers used a process called bluing. When iron was heated, a layer of oxide was created on the surface that would turn it blue, gray, or purple.

An all-season style dedicated to the eternal power of ice.

"I am the whisper in the wind, the cold embrace that descends as night falls. It is I who sculpted the great rocks of this earth, I who carved its mountains and valleys. It is I who yield the power to cast a silent, numbing shroud over all that lives, to plunge this world into a deep, dreamless sleep. I have seen the rise and fall of great empires, entire civilizations lost in the ebb and flow of time. I have witnessed all: I am eternal, a force from long before the age of men, and one that will endure long after it."
An all-season style dedicated to the unstoppable force of water.

"Few comprehend the true scale of my power. Fewer still realize how fortunate they are that I am a merciful being, that I choose not to utilize my might to its fullest extent. For if I did, I would unleash upon this world a cataclysm the like of which it has never seen before. I command this planet's lifeblood: from the pulsating tides of its endless oceans to the raging torrents of its great rivers. Maelstroms, tempests, deluges—all are the work of my omnipotent hand. This fragile planet is my dominion, and I alone have the power to change life on it beyond all recognition."
An all-season style available for purchase for fans of fierce clan battles.
An all-season style awarded to the winners of the special clan event.
An all-season style awarded to the participants of the final stage of the special clan event.
An all-season style that celebrates team camaraderie.

Your team is about belonging. It's about unity, resilience, and having no fear. Because when you're with your people, there's nothing to fear. You play to each other's strengths and bring out the best in each other. You're free to express yourself—because you know your teammates will always have your back, no matter what. You've been through a lot—good times and bad. But all the hours spent training together, honing strategies through victory and defeat—they were worth it. Because they've made you unbreakable—and ready for anything.
An all-season style dedicated to the bow of Apollo, god of light and prophecy.

The golden bow of Apollo—Olympian god of light, prophecy, archery, and more—is a central weapon in Greek mythology. Crafted by the divine blacksmith Hephaestus, it was bestowed upon Apollo in his youth to defend his mother, Leto, from the monstrous serpent Python. From that moment on, Apollo bore the bow as a guardian of order and an agent of divine justice, striking from afar with unerring precision and arrows that could inspire love or unleash plague—all depending on his will.
An all-season style dedicated to the three-pointed spear of the warrior deity, Erlang Shen.

The three-pointed, double-edged spear—also known as the Divine Spear—wielded by the warrior deity Erlang Shen is one of the most revered weapons in all of Chinese mythology. As befits a champion of Erlang's renown and cosmic authority, it is not merely an instrument of war, but a tool of divine justice, intricately forged and capable of piercing through evil and illusion alike. Battling legions of demons and malevolent spirits, Erlang commands the spear with unparalleled dexterity and grace—even as he confronts his most formidable adversary: the Monkey King, Sun Wukong.
An all-season style dedicated to Excalibur, the mythical sword of King Arthur.

The mythical sword of the great King Arthur, the very name Excalibur has echoed through the legends of Britain for centuries. So profound is its mystery that even the tales of its origin offer no single truth: some say the young king drew it from a stone, proving his divine right to rule; others that it was gifted to him by the enigmatic Lady of the Lake. However it was won, Excalibur's power surpassed any blade forged in the realms of men—and spoke of the valor and noble spirit of the king who wielded it.
An all-season style dedicated to Mjölnir, hammer of the thunder god Thor.

Forged by the dwarf brothers Sindri and Brokkr as part of a bet with the trickster god Loki, the mighty Mjölnir is the hammer of Thor, master of thunder and lightning. A symbol of divine power and a shield against darkness, it safeguarded the realms of Asgard and Midgard from giants and other malevolent forces. Heavier than any mortal weapon and nigh-on indestructible, a single blow from Mjölnir could shatter mountains and summon almighty storms—and, no matter how far the hammer was thrown, it always returned to its master's hand.

They have no idea of the rage simmering beneath their feet. The land in the valley has not trembled for four centuries, but who gave the humans here the right to desecrate these slopes, steal resources, and build their primitive dwellings as though in derision of nature? Their existence is so fragile, so insignificant, yet they dare to threaten me, an immortal guardian. Well, they will soon realize their folly. The flame raging within me will burst out into the world and consume everything in its path, for I am Vulcan, I am destruction, and no one can challenge me. Let the humans tremble with fear. After all, they have awakened the beast and they must pay for it.
An all-season style inspired by the legend of the Jade Rabbit.

One day, the Jade Emperor sought help from a noble animal to prepare the elixir of life, for humans were not to be trusted. He wandered the forest disguised as a beggar, crying out for food. The monkey, the fox, and the rabbit heard his plea. The monkey gathered fruit, the fox hunted fish, but the rabbit found nothing but grass. Wanting to help, he leaped into the fire as an offering. Moved by this selfless act, the Jade Emperor saved the rabbit and carried him to the moon. If you look up at the markings on the full moon, you might still be able to see the Jade Rabbit at work.
An all season-style inspired by the legend of the Ten Suns.

Long ago, the legend says, there were ten suns that took turns illuminating the Earth. As time went by, they grew tired of their routine and decided to go up into the sky together. But when they all shone at once, their tenfold power wrought great havoc. Lakes and rivers began to dry up, crops wilted, and people and animals alike sought refuge from the unbearable heat. The world would have been lost, if not for a skilled archer. He shot nine suns down—but spared the last one to provide light and warmth. From that time, there has been just one sun in the sky.
Celebrate armored vehicles in all their glory with this all-season style.

Where would we be without tanks, and how better to honor these majestic machines than to sport their likeness on the battlefield? Set against a radiant golden backdrop, the image of a modern tank proudly adorns contemporary and historical armor alike. Like a knight's pennant, let it serve as a personal banner for your vehicle.
An all-season style dedicated to those who protect their brothers in arms from high above.

Amid explosions and gunfire, tank crews have always found solace in the roar above—watchful eyes soaring high, ready to strike at a moment’s notice. From early propellers to the silent speed of modern jets, aviation has reshaped the battlefield, bringing devastation for some and protection for others. This style honors the relentless pursuit of innovation, where steel on the ground and wings in the sky move as one, pushing ever forward into a new age of warfare.

An all-season style dedicated to Labor Day.

Labor Day is celebrated on May 1 in 142 countries. For decades, this day had political subtext. It was always associated with parades; posters; portraits of political figures; strike workers; and banners with information on achievements in some sector of agriculture, science, or culture.

In some countries, the tradition of hosting parades under union banners still takes place, but most countries celebrating it treat it like just another summer holiday. Ironically, Labor Day is often a day off with celebratory parades, open-air parties, and concerts. For many people, it is an opportunity to take a break, take care of themselves, or spend time with their families.
An all-season style inspired by one of the traditional Chinese festivals.

New Year celebrations in China always end with the Lantern Festival. It is held on the 15th day of the first lunar calendar month and is considered one of the biggest events of the year for locals. During the festival, people enjoy the full moon, watch fireworks, solve riddles, eat sweet rice balls called Tangyuan, and light millions of lanterns of amazing shapes and sizes.
An exclusive style for Huya Live.

A special style dedicated to the Huya Live streaming platform. This style's origin is shown through the use of Huya’s orange-and-brown color scheme and elements, as well as multiple images of the Huya mascot across the hull.
An all-season style developed to celebrate Lunar New Year, a traditional spring festival in China.

The order of things in nature is unchangeable and known to everyone. It is an eternal cycle of blossoming and decay. It is true that after blossoming comes decay. But after decay also comes blossoming, which is equally true, but it does not have a grim undertone. Such is the tiger's wisdom: without changing the order of things, learn to look at them from another angle.

Many countries in Asia celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar. The origin of the Mid-Autumn Festival comes from the legend of Chang'e, a beautiful woman who took an immortality potion and ascended to the Moon Palace, unwittingly separating herself from her family forever. As an offering to Chang'e, who was condemned to live a life of solitude in the Moon Palace, her family began to place balls of rice flour and platters of fresh fruit in their garden. These traditions spread widely, transforming into a custom of worshipping the moon and eating mooncakes during the Mid-Autumn Festival. From mythological stories to ancient books and frescoes, Chang'e has become a symbol of the Mid-Autumn Festival. Now, these celebrations in her honor have turned into a time for family reunions.
An all-season style dedicated to the National Day of the People's Republic of China.

On October 1, 1949, a ceremony celebrating the forming of the Central People's Government took place on Tiananmen Square in Beijing. Later, this date was declared National Day of the People's Republic of China and it became the main national holiday of the country. On this day, festivities and concerts are held all over China, and the holiday ends with fireworks at night. Public places are decorated in a festive theme and portraits of revered leaders are publicly displayed.

An all-season style inspired by "The Mystery of the Third Planet", a Soviet animated science fiction film produced in 1981 based on the novella "Alice's Travel" by Kir Bulychev.
An all-season style dedicated to the human aspiration to explore the endless expanse of space.

This style is based on the thermal-protective coating used on reusable spacecraft. Such a coating consists of more than 31,000 separate lightweight silica tiles that expand under heat and protect the integrity of the internal hull. This coating is relatively easy to maintain: if a tile is damaged or torn off, only that tile needs replacing instead of needing to repair the craft's entire body.
A unique all-season style developed to celebrate Cosmonautics Day.

From the moment humanity overcame gravity, we have been striving to break away from the ground towards the millions of stars, galaxies, or even universes out there. We want to believe that we will never lose the beauty of the night sky and twinkling stars, still as beautiful and mysterious as in the first days of creation.
An all-season style that represents the infinite and unexplored space beyond Earth's atmosphere.
An a-moo-sing all-season style to help you stand out from the herd.

Holy cow! You'd need to have nerves of veal to sport this udderly unexpected camouflage on the battlefield. It's certainly a bold moo-ve in tactical fashion, but the looks on your allies' faces would be legen-dairy. Plus, you can really milk the element of surprise while the enemy struggles to bull-ieve what they're looking at. Before they can recalibrate, your oddly dressed armor will have already grazed past their defenses. Anyway, that's enough ruminating. It's time to focus up and roll out into cattle! Ahem. Battle.
A unique style, awarded to players for personal and clan achievements on the Global Map.

They speak of a place where the wind turned red—where the earth drank deep, and the leaves became embers in the fading light. None saw the samurai pass. Yet when the wind stirs, the whisper of his blade still cuts the silence.
So the elders murmur, and the scrolls recall—a silent warrior painted in fading ink, his armor dulled by time, his name lost to history. His battle lies buried, his tale near-forgotten... yet his vow endures. For not in the name of glory did he draw his sword, but of duty unspoken and honor undying. When the wind rises, heed it well—the crimson wind still bears his oath.
An all-season style honoring the age-old art of crafting iron ore into instruments of war.

From the forests of Bohemia to the peaks of the Tatras, these lands have long been a crucible of craftsmanship. Centuries ago, the clank of hammers on anvils echoed through medieval streets as smiths wrought the swords, axes, and spears that would write the story of their age in battle. Now, the sounds of industry are the roar of furnaces and the whir of machines that forge the hulking tanks of modern battlefields. The artisans of that bygone era would hardly recognize these mechanized war horses. But it was their ingenuity and dedication to their craft that paved the way for their creation.

The veteran tank that saw many battles. Following the liberation of another city, the commander ordered the crew to prepare the vehicle for a commemorative parade along the main street. The tank was honorably decorated in the colors of the Czechoslovakian national hero—Jan Žižka.
An all-season style dedicated to the daring Allied landings of Operation Overlord.

Unprecedented in its scale, Operation Overlord turned the tide of World War II decisively in the Allies' favor. Supported by over 5,000 ships and landing craft to bolster their audacious assault, almost 160,000 Allied troops landed on five heavily defended beaches on June 6, 1944, in a bold effort to breach German lines. Over the following days, the Allies pushed deeper into occupied territory, weakening Germany's grip on Western Europe and enshrining the windswept beaches of Normandy in history as the site of one of the most daring military operations ever seen.
An all-season style inspired by Mexican folk art.

Alebrijes are a special style of Mexican art. The first brightly colored alebrije toys were made in Mexico City by Pedro Linares. In 1936, Linares had a strong fever and dreamed of fantastical colorful animals with horns, tails, wings, and fangs, who kept repeating the word "Alebrijes!". When the artist recovered, he made sculptures based on them, which, with time, became incredibly popular even outside of Mexico. Nowadays, alebrije figures made of papier-mâché, cardboard, and wood are sold all over the world. Usually, they depict fictional creatures, animals, people, and skeletons.

An all-season style to commemorate the annual holiday for remembering the dead on November 1–2. The holiday, which is celebrated in Mexico and other Latin American countries, can trace its roots to the Aztecs and other indigenous peoples. It is believed that the souls of the dead awaken and return to the living world to their loved ones. In turn, their living family members treat the deceased as honored guests and provide the deceased's favorite foods and other items as offerings.
A unique all-season style developed to celebrate Defender's Day.

Russian winters have played a key role in many military campaigns over the years. During the Great Northern War from 1700–1721, extreme cold destroyed almost a half of the Swedish army of King Charles XII. In 1812, sub-zero temperatures cooled off Napoleon's army, and the winter of 1941–1942 brought the German Blitzkrieg strategy to a halt. The generals of Western European armies often state the piercing cold as the main reason of their defeats. Soldiers were falling ill and equipment stopped working. Because of this, a fictional General Frost was created to personify the Russian winter that snatched the victories from the hands of enemy.
A top-secret, all-season style, developed using technological innovations in vehicle armor.
An all-season style based on "Digital Vegetato", an Italian camouflage pattern.

An all-season style based on "Digital Vegetato", an Italian camouflage pattern that is associated with an abandoned vehicle covered in rust and wear scars. It is difficult to detect such a target in the autumn woods. Even if this vehicle is spotted, it can be easily taken for a destroyed tank rather than a fully operational one, giving its crew an advantage on the battlefield.

A camouflage pattern used by the 7th Armored Division of the British Army, which played an active role in the Western Desert Campaign during World War II. For their exploits, its tankers gained the Desert Rats nickname.

The Fremen are the inhabitants of the desert planet Arrakis, also known as Dune. They have adapted to the harsh desert environment and are skilled in survival techniques. In a world where survival is earned with each footstep, the Fremen stride. Walking without rhythm, their footsteps echo like a drum in the vast expanse of the unforgiving sands.
A unique style, awarded to players for personal and clan achievements on the Global Map.

An all-season style based on a special camouflage pattern used by the Navy during World War I. This camouflage did not conceal a ship but made it difficult for the enemy to estimate a target's range, speed, and heading.
Bring the might of a legendary protector to the battlefield with this fierce all-season style.

"When prejudice rears its ugly head,
Gaze upon my own instead.
For I, though ghastly to behold,
Champion those left outside the fold."

Blessed with stunning intellect yet cursed with a beastly appearance, scholar Zhong Kui was shunned in his mortal life. It was only after his untimely demise that he could fight the kind of injustice he had once endured, ridding the world of evil with supernatural force.
Unfurl this serene all-season style like a painted scroll.

"Calm waters bear proud vessels,
Dwarfed by looming mountains,
That bow beneath engulfing clouds,
Fated to pour back down.

Though still, Commander, my images are not stationary. Follow the ink as it flows from calm pools to great peaks, to the heavens, and back. There is a lesson to be learned here. You see, each battle is but one stroke on your canvas. Whatever the outcome, it is merely a single line in a story still unfolding. The brush does not fall from your hand unless you release it."
An all-season style dedicated to Qu Yuan, a Chinese poet.

The Dragon Boat Festival is closely tied to Qu Yuan. A descendant of aristocrats, he was serving the state of Chu as its Left Minister and could influence its politics, but he was exiled as a result of a conspiracy by corrupt ministers. Saddened by the fate of his country, he found consolation in art and wrote dozens of poems.
In 278 B.C., most of the Chu state was captured by the Qin army. Overburdened with grief and his own powerlessness, Qu Yuan waded into the river and, according to legend, later returned as a spirit and said that the reason for his death was the river dragon. Later, the poet's memory was commemorated with the Duanwu festival, the main event of which is a rowing competition on boats with dragon heads.
An all-season style inspired by Chinese art.

One Chinese legend says that cranes can fly between the real world and the spirit realm. They escort the dead to the heavens, carry immortals on their wings, and carry out the will of the gods on Earth as wanderers. The crane is very important in the cultures and mythologies of different countries. In art, cranes symbolize longevity and peace, and they can be seen in the paintings of many famous artists.

Oh, how ssweet the moment will be when they learn, when they reap what they themsselvess ssowed. Ssome will receive the wissdom of the agess, the ssecret knowledge. As for the otherss... Abssolute annihilation!"
An all-season style that pays tribute to the unbridled might of the mythological dragon king.

"Fear not the lóngwáng—the dragon king—for he is a benevolent deity. But respect him; sovereign of the aquatic realm and the vast seas that surround us, he has the power to summon either life-giving rains or devastating tempests, if such be his will. The ever-flowing rivers of our verdant land, the lakes that shimmer in the mountain moonlight, the wide oceans and great seas—all are the dominion of the lóngwáng, and our mightiest battleships, our proudest junks are but paper vessels within it. So we thank the protector for granting us safe passage through the most troubled of waters, today and every day."
Like the koi who became a dragon, defy all odds in this all-season style.

The Yellow River shimmered with a vast school of golden carp. They fought the current, pushing upstream until they reached a towering waterfall—too high, it seemed, to overcome. Many turned back, while some attempted to leap the obstacle and failed, swept back downstream as the spirits of the celestial realm looked on.

In time, one fish prevailed. It dove deep, gathered all its strength, and surged skyward, clearing the falls at last. For this feat, the fish was transformed into a dragon, the heavens' reward for its tenacity.
The elements converge in this tempestuous all-season style.

The heaving deep runs wild and blue,
its foaming crests come crashing through.
White spray crowns each rising gale,
then breaks, revealing burnished scale.

A flicker bright as molten gold
slips through the tide in twisting fold.
It coils where darker waters run,
a serpent flashing in the sun.

The storm may roar, the waves may break,
but gold keeps glinting in their wake.
A dragon turning out of sight,
Laced through the sea in sparks of light.

In times of old, mapmakers would mark the edges of the known world with the phrase "Here be dragons" and images of fearsome mythical beasts as warnings of the dangers that lurked in hitherto uncharted regions. Yet little did they know that dragons dwell not only in the farthest reaches of the earth, but much closer indeed. Deep within ancient mountains and forgotten ruins, their molten eyes glint in the blackness, the pulse of their fiery breath punctuating the silence—hidden from the gaze of mortals, they bide their time, waiting to emerge once more.
An all-season style developed to commemorate the celebration of Easter.

For hundreds of years, the bunny has been considered a traditional symbol of Easter by Catholics. The same meaning for this fluffy animal was used by Ambrose of Milan, a preacher, theologian, and a poet. For him, a bunny who changed the color of its fur with the cycle of the seasons became a symbol of Christ's regeneration.
In the U.S. and Europe, parents prepare for the holiday in advance. Easter eggs that are "brought" by bunnies are hidden carefully in the house or outside, and children start the day looking for the eggs. There is also a tradition of giving kids chocolate and marzipan bunnies on this day.

"We remain in memory only as our deeds. The martial art we've been learning since the day we were born is like a sharp blade that remains in its sheath, always ready to battle for what is good and right. As long as the sun blesses the fields with its warmth, as long as the fields are worked, and as long as peace and justice prevail in our lands, we continue to hone our spirits and our bodies. Yes, we were born and raised for battle. Yes, this is our purpose. The memories and the pride of our ancestors. Yet it is best for our swords to remain in their sheaths. We may be remembered for our deeds, but those deeds don't have to forever be war."

The blueish-gray eyes of the war elephant looked into the distance. Its body was covered in scars, reminders of battles past. Its heart was full of rage, and its ears were ringing from the thunder of weapons and war cries. It knew that wars had left no place for kindness and justice inside it. This beast had been trained ever since it was born. Trained so that the crimson euphoria of a violent battle became the meaning of its entire life. Here it stood again, on the front line. Encased in massive gold-plated armor, ready to do what it knows best: STOMP!
An all-season style developed to celebrate Christmas and New Year's Day.

The Red Hat Battalion deploys every year along the state borders to repel potential attacks from Krampus, whose forces become suspiciously active just before the end of December. As long as the the borders are secure and our brave soldiers are valiantly keeping their watch, the holidays are safe.
An all-season style inspired by the confrontation between Great Britain and the revolutionaries of the 13 colonies during the Revolutionary War (1775–1783).

In the early years of the War of Independence, American farmers and craftsmen—who comprised a significant part of the Continental Army—were often defeated by the British military. New York was captured a year into the war, and Philadelphia was lost some time after that.
The victory at the Battles of Saratoga in October 1777 is considered a turning point for American patriots. Equally important was the signing of the Franco-American Treaty. Later, Spain joined the list of European allies, and the Russian Empire issued the Declaration of Armed Neutrality, which was convenient for the American colonies.
A decisive victory for the Americans took place at the Battle of Yorktown in 1781. Great Britain could no longer keep on suppressing resistance in the colonies. They laid down their arms and entered negotiations. Two years later, Great Britain signed a treaty recognizing the independence of the United States.
A futuristic all-season style dedicated to the reality-warping world of Neon Dash.

"I've seen things you people wouldn't believe. Hell, I didn't believe it myself when they gave the order. I grew up watching those goofy '80s sci-fi movies, dreaming of a world I'd never see. And then I got in. Portal to another dimension. Neon world. Race to the finish. None of it made sense. I'm a tanker, not a racing driver—or I was, before I came here. But things in here don't work like they do out there, and I'm not the same person I was before. I've freed my mind. And I suggest you do too."
What's Christmas without fireworks? Besides, the person who arranges it brings the festive spirit to the whole neighborhood.
A unique all-season style, received for completing the Lunar New Year collection during the Holiday Ops 2019 event.
A unique all-season style, received for completing the Lunar New Year collection during the Holiday Ops 2019 event. It brings back the Festive Atmosphere to your Garage. No restrictions on nations.

Ever feel like your life's a film, and you're the main character? Sometimes you find yourself in a situation so surreal, so absurd, that it can't possibly be real. You're just watching absolute madness unfold around you in real time and thinking to yourself, "How the hell did I get here?". And honestly, some of the characters you meet doing what we do, they're larger than life. Arms dealers, bounty hunters, bare-knuckle fighters, caravan peddlers—people whose stories are so unbelievable, you'd think they must be out of a film or something. But life imitates art, I suppose, doesn't it?
Bring the heat and cook on the battlefield with this red-hot all-season style.
An all-season style developed to commemorate April Fools' Day celebrated on April 1.
